texts: I don't just build worlds; I craft experiences that challenge, delight, and captivate players.

I am a highly effective Mobile Game Designer specializing in delivering high-retention content across diverse puzzle and logic mechanics. Over the past 4+ years, I have designed and implemented over 1,500 unique levels, focusing on meticulously crafted difficulty curves and mechanical depth that drive long-term player engagement.
My expertise spans multiple genres, including physics-based bullet puzzles, creative construction challenges, logic puzzles, observation games, and detective mysteries. I have designed 400+ levels of progressive ricochet puzzles, 200+ creative drawing levels, and 300+ IQ-testing logic puzzles.

Designed and structured the core gameplay experiences for Krishna, developing diverse mini-games integrated across multiple maps. Owned the complete gameplay loop, defining mechanics, content pacing, difficulty balancing, and level progression to maintain an optimal gameplay flow. Synthesized narrative integration with targeted reward systems and retention-driven design to sustain player motivation and long-term engagement.

Designed and executed multiple new mini-games, handling end-to-end mechanics, puzzle-driven level design, and feature implementation. Supported character design alongside creating 2D character and gameplay animations, UI assets, and core visual elements. Drove progression balancing, rigorous testing, and continuous iteration to deliver a polished, high-quality player experience.

Level design for the core Eraser puzzle loop of The Eraser's Pursuit was centered on maximizing player retention and fostering a deep sense of player investment. The level progression was meticulously crafted with a seamless difficulty curve, unconsciously teaching advanced strategies and meta-gameplay to keep players highly engaged and motivated to complete each stage.

The 500-level design focuses on two core ideas: a smooth difficulty progression and learning without explicit instruction. New mechanics are introduced gradually, so players naturally understand the game as they play. This keeps the challenge balanced with their skill, maintaining a steady flow and improving retention, with around 0.2% of users reaching level 500

This is a puzzle game where players must cut ropes to guide a civilian to safety. It uses a high-retention level design that teaches new mechanics organically, without tutorials. A challenging boss level is unlocked after every five puzzles, providing a strong sense of accomplishment and a powerful incentive to keep players engaged and motivated.. they learn how to manipulate momentum, utilize environmental physics, and orchestrate precise chain reactions.

This is a 2D physics-based puzzle shooter for mobile, with 200+ levels. where players control a secret agent who must eliminate all enemies using a ricocheting bullet. The game is built around clever problem-solving, with levels that require players to bounce their shot off walls and interact with environmental elements like bombs, switches, and movable planks to create chain reactions this makes the game highly engaging for mobile audiences.
Game Design Document for Bullet Game

As a core content designer for Detective IQ 1, the primary work involved creating and implementing content across 20 distinct mini-games designed to maximize player retention. This included developing 400+ levels for the physics-based shooter (Mr. Bullet), 200+ levels for the creative drawing puzzle (Draw to Save), and designing the 50-60 logical Gameplay levels for the each minigame. The focus was on delivering a massive volume of varied, high-quality content to ensure continuous player engagement and skill mastery.

The work focused on designing and structuring the core logic puzzles in Detective IQ 1. This involved:
-Detective Cases (50-60 levels): Designing deduction scenarios that require players to find all hidden clues and logically synthesize the evidence to clear the case.
-Flashback (30-40 levels): Developing observation puzzles using the time control mechanic, challenging players to identify critical, fleeting visual evidence by rewinding and forwarding the scene.

My core contribution was the design and implementation of over 400 unique levels for the Bullet physics-based shooter. This content was progressively structured for fine gameplay and mechanical mastery, teaching players to utilize environmental interactions (triggering bombs, shattering planks, etc) to clear each stage using a single, calculated bullet. This high-volume, quality-controlled approach resulted in achieving a 0.5% user retention rate at level 400.

My contribution involved designing and implementing over 200 levels for the Draw to Save mini-game. This gameplay focuses on creative drawing and physics-based problem-solving, where players must manually draw lines to create structures that safeguard a civilian from immediate danger. The work concentrated on designing progressively complex environmental hazards that demanded flexible and imaginative solutions, ensuring a large volume of content that tests player creativity and spatial reasoning.

The central design responsibility was creating and implementing over 180+ unique puzzle levels for Pizza IQ: Brain Game. The core challenge involved strictly adhering to a pizza-centric theme while demanding solutions based on both logical deduction and out-of-the-box thinking. The work focused on structuring the content for progressive difficulty, ensuring the high-volume levels consistently tested player IQ and spatial reasoning using limited, thematically constrained assets in inventive and tricky ways.

Wobble Bomber

Wobble Bomber is a 5v5 ragdoll physics elimination game. Players secretly position themselves before seven bombs spawn. Once a bomb is grabbed, the carrier has five seconds to throw it or self-detonate. Strategic gameplay centers on using "Flail" knockbacks to push enemies into blasts and leveraging green bushes for stealth. Symmetrical maps feature teleporters and gray walls for tactical flanking. A dynamic spawning system adjusts bomb frequency to player count, while a Poison Cloud shrinks the arena to force final combat. Success requires managing a three-hit health system across five rounds.

DreamLink: The Fractured Timeline 

DreamLink: The Fractured Timeline is a two-player co-operative puzzle game where two players inhabit the fractured consciousness of a single person—one in the logical Reality (R) realm and the other in the rule-bending Dream (D) realm. The core mechanic is inter-dimensional synchronization: players must communicate and coordinate actions in their respective worlds (e.g., a switch press in R creates a bridge in D) to solve complex puzzles and progress. The narrative drives the gameplay, compelling the players to merge their broken timeline before the division becomes permanent, revealing they are subjects of a failed temporal experiment.
